messages:
maya: quick heads-up — I'm bringing up a new embed candidate 'emberlyn-v1'. did a smoke recall@10 on the wiki holdout and saw a ~3.3% absolute drop vs beacon-v2. dropping the summary here and links to artifacts.
omar: ouch. can you paste the short summary numbers and exactly which configs you ran?
maya: summary paste below:
```
baseline: beacon-v2 (fp16)  recall@10 = 0.642
emberlyn-v1 fp16             recall@10 = 0.609  (-0.033)
emberlyn-v1 int8 (per-channel) recall@10 = 0.618 (-0.024)
NDCG@5: baseline 0.712 -> emberlyn-fp16 0.691
average cosine sim (pos pairs): baseline 0.78 -> emberlyn 0.75
```
ran on wiki-holdout (10k queries), k=10, L2-normalized vectors after generation. command: `python -m eval.run --model emberlyn-v1 --holdout wiki --k 10 --norm l2 --quant int8 --seed 42` artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/emberlyn/v1/*
sasha: any cohort breakdown? short queries vs long? lang?
maya: yes — cohort split: shortseq (<8 tokens) drop is worst: recall@10 down 6.5% absolute on shortseq. long queries (>25 tokens) basically parity. en / non-en both show small dip but shortseq en dominates the signal.
chris: interesting. did you check cosine vs dot? maybe scale/mean changed (layernorm tweak?)
maya: tried both cosine+norm and raw dot; the relative drop persists. also plotted similarity histogram — looks like positives' mean shifted left by ~0.03 and variance up.
eric: could be embedding magnitude variance from changed layernorm or last-layer pooling. any architecture diff vs beacon?
maya: emberlyn changes: replaced mean-pool with rotary-pooling at last layer + moved final LN before projection. small change but plausible.
omar: try whitening/centering postproc? sometimes new center offset hurts small queries.
maya: quick experiment: applied mean-centering (compute mean on train index, subtract) + renormalize -> recall@10 for fp16 recovered to 0.631 (still -0.011 vs baseline). int8+centering -> 0.626. so centering helps but doesn't fully close gap.
sasha: what about kNN id-flips? do top1 neighbors change or are positives still in top10 just lower rank?
maya: more id-flip than pure rank-shift. for many queries the ground-truth neighbor moved from rank 1 to rank 5-12. nearest neighbor recall@1 dropped a lot on shortseq.
chris: clustering/umap? maybe small segments collapsed differently.
maya: ran UMAP on 2k shortseq queries + their positives; clusters look more diffuse. here's gist with the scatter: https://gist.github.com/maya/emberlyn-umap (notes in the gist).
eric: quantization effect looks smaller (int8 only -0.009 vs fp16). might be model change not quant noise. but we should still try per-channel calibration sweep and symmetric vs asymmetric.
omar: also try pre-whiten (PCA-whiten) — sometimes normalization interacts with pooling changes.
maya: agreed. plan: 1) run per-channel int8 calibration sweep (symmetric/asym, scale methods) 2) run whitening + re-eval on shortseq / longtail cohorts 3) produce nearest-neighbor id-flip diff report (topk overlap matrix) 4) sanity-check dot vs cosine distributions. I'll kick off jobs and post artifacts.
ci-bot: nightly-eval pipeline started: job id emberlyn-v1-eval-20260402-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/emberlyn-v1-eval-20260402-01/logs
sasha: can you also include intra-query variance plot (embedding norm distribution) and a small sample of cases where ground-truth moved out of top10? good to show examples for model folks.
maya: yes. adding that to artifacts. also will run an ablation replicate that sets final LN back to pre-projection to test hypothesis.
eric: if centering mostly helps, might be safe to add an indexing postproc step as fallback while we iterate. but prefer fixing model if performance improves with minimal cost.
omar: agree. for Dedicated customers we can ship index-time whitening as a config knob. for hosted we should be careful.
maya: update: started calibration sweep, ETA ~45m. will post interim table once first 5 runs finish. thanks all :thumbsup:
chris: thanks — let us know if you want help interpreting id-flip matrix (I can run the pairwise overlap script)
maya: will ping. closing for now, will update thread when results land.
